newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil barges easier, cargoes firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil barges easier, cargoes firmer.

text.p: NWE barges were easier on slack demand on Monday but cargoes were notionally firmer on forecasts of colder weather, traders said.
Jan IPE benchmark futures were $3 firmer at $216.75 a tonne in light featureless trade.
Barges of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil refinery grade traded at Jan IPE -$1 fob Rotterdam, around $1 easier, for second half December but buyers were rare.
"The market is barely in existence, because most buyers are busy wrapping up the operational side of the first half (of December) and then there is the Christmas lull," a trader said.
Offers of low sulphur diesel French grade was around Jan IPE +$11 but there were no bids.
On cargoes, heating oil material into Hamburg was bid around Jan IPE +$5.50/6 with offers notionally around $7.
Gas oil was helped by Weather Services Corporation (WSC) forecasts that cold weather could hit the key heating oil market of the northeast United States by the weekend.
In Europe WSC forecast above normal temperatures in northwest Europe in the next 10 days but in northeast Europe temperatures were seen below normal into the next five days.
